definitions.explanation: To physically separate something by cutting.
To separate things or concepts that were previously connected.

examples.japanese: {枝|えだ}を{切|き}り{離|はな}した。
ロープを{切|き}り{離|はな}して{船|ふね}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I cut the rope and sent the boat off.

examples.japanese: {故障|こしょう}した{部品|ぶひん}を{本体|ほんたい}から{切|き}り{離|はな}す。
examples.english: To detach the broken part from the main unit.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}を{起|お}こした{車両|しゃりょう}を{編成|へんせい}から{切|き}り{離|はな}して、{残|のこ}りの{電車|でんしゃ}を{運行|うんこう}させた。
examples.english: They detached the car involved in the accident from the train and ran the remaining cars.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}と{私生活|しせいかつ}を{切|き}り{離|はな}す。
examples.english: To separate work and private life.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}は{切|き}り{離|はな}して{考|かんが}えよう。
{感情|かんじょう}と{事実|じじつ}を{切|き}り{離|はな}して{判断|はんだん}する。
examples.english: To judge by separating emotions from facts.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}の{問題|もんだい}と{環境|かんきょう}の{問題|もんだい}は{切|き}り{離|はな}せない{関係|かんけい}にある。
examples.english: Economic issues and environmental issues are inseparably related.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{文化|ぶんか}を{歴史|れきし}から{切|き}り{離|はな}して{理解|りかい}することはできない。
examples.english: You cannot understand Japanese culture in isolation from its history.

notes:
{切|き}り{離|はな}す means to cut off and separate, either physically or figuratively.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を for the thing being separated

COMPOUND VERB:
Formed from {切|き}る (to cut) + {離|はな}す (to separate/release).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AをBから{切|き}り{離|はな}す: to separate A from B
- {仕事|しごと}と{私生活|しせいかつ}を{切|き}り{離|はな}す: to separate work and private life
- {切|き}り{離|はな}して{考|かんが}える: to consider separately
- {切|き}り{離|はな}せない{関係|かんけい}: inseparable relationship

ASPECT (ている):
{切|き}り{離|はな}している indicates an ongoing state of separation.

PASSIVE:
{切|き}り{離|はな}される: to be cut off, to be separated
